themes.label: Household sharing blocks legitimate users
themes.summary: Users across iOS reviews say Netflix's household policy is locking out people who live apart, including college students, travelers, and family members at another home, often requiring an extra screen or paid account to keep access. Many describe the restriction as punishing paying customers, with the price increases and the ads tier making the change feel like a money grab, and several are cancelling or downgrading. The complaints span versions from 2023 to 2026, suggesting the policy has been a persistent source of anger rather than a single bug.
themes.recommendation: Audit household verification failure logs by reason (device not on home network, device count exceeded, travel-pass expiry) and measure how often paying members are blocked in the 30 days before cancellation, then prioritize a fix such as a longer or renewable travel pass or a lower-cost extra member slot.

themes.label: Playback failures and loading on phone
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS report that videos hang on loading, buffer endlessly, freeze, or fail to play on their phones, while the same account often works on TV or laptop. Many reviews are recent Android builds around v9.7x to v9.8x, and several say the app stalls on the loading screen or shows "can't connect" errors, with some reinstalling and clearing cache without success.
themes.recommendation: Pull crash, playback-error, and loading-timeout logs segmented by Android build (v9.73.0 through v9.83.0) and phone-only versus TV, then compare against the video player and network stack changes shipped in those releases to identify a regression and a rollback or hotfix candidate.

themes.label: Titles removed and seasons missing
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android are frustrated that Netflix frequently removes shows, movies, and individual seasons, sometimes mid-episode or mid-movie, and that partial seasons leave series unfinished. Many want a say in which titles stay, or a longer window to finish what they started, and several say the removals push them toward other services or cancellations.
themes.recommendation: Audit the iOS and Android removal and season-availability pipelines to find why partial seasons go live and why titles vanish mid-playback, then ship a warning and grace period so in-progress titles are not cut off abruptly.

themes.label: Login and sign-in failures across devices
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS report being unable to sign in, with errors like "Something went wrong" and "Too many people are using your account" appearing even after password resets or fresh installs. Several also describe phone number or email verification failing during sign-up and payment, and some say they cannot reach the account settings needed to cancel. Many reviewers have already cancelled or deleted the app, and a few mention a security concern about an account accessed without their knowledge.
themes.recommendation: Pull auth and error logs for the "Something went wrong" and "Too many people are using your account" responses, segmented by app version 9.70 to 9.84 and by sign-in method (email, phone, code), and fix the phone and email verification path during sign-up and payment.

themes.label: Rising subscription prices and cancellations
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS say the monthly subscription has become too expensive for the library they get, citing repeated price increases, ads on paid tiers, and a thin or aging catalogue with titles leaving the service. Many mention they have downgraded, cancelled, or are weighing free alternatives. A smaller group pairs the price complaint with app bugs such as freezing, playback resets, and lost watch position.
themes.recommendation: Pull churn and downgrade data for the last two price increases by region and plan tier, and test whether a lower-priced or ad-supported tier with a clearly stated catalogue value retains cancelling users.

themes.label: Chromecast casting removed in update
themes.summary: Android users report that after the early September 2026 update (v9.82.0), the cast button disappeared from the Netflix app, breaking casting to Chromecast devices including older models without remotes. Many say casting worked fine with other streaming apps on the same device and network, and several threaten to cancel or switch services, with some saying support confirmed the feature is no longer supported.
themes.recommendation: Investigate whether the cast button removal in v9.82.0 was intentional or a regression by diffing cast-related code and feature flags between v9.81.0 and v9.82.0, then restore or clearly communicate Chromecast support for older devices without remotes.

themes.label: Playback resumes at wrong position
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS, including several on TV apps, report that Netflix does not resume shows where they left off. Playback often restarts from the beginning, jumps back an episode or more, or shows the wrong last-watched title, and some say watch progress fails to sync between the phone app and a TV. Reviewers note the problem is intermittent but frustrating, and several mention having to manually search for their position.
themes.recommendation: Investigate the resume-position sync pipeline by reproducing pause, app-background, and cross-device handoff on Android (v9.80 to v9.83) and iOS, and check whether stored watch progress is overwritten or delayed by the client on return from background.

themes.label: Removed titles and content gaps
themes.summary: Users across this iOS cluster repeatedly say Netflix cancels or removes shows and movies they love, often with little notice, and that titles they want to rewatch disappear while less-liked ones stay. Many also want a dedicated teen section between the kids and adult profiles, and several say ratings like PG or TV-Y7 sometimes hide mature content. Some mention the difficulty of finding titles in recently watched and the lack of expiring-soon warnings.
themes.recommendation: Investigate the title licensing removal cadence for the top-requested removed titles and add an expiring-soon notice in the watchlist and title detail screen, then scope a teen profile tier (ages 13-16) with its own rating filter for PG-13 and TV-14 content.

themes.label: Praise: broad catalogue and ease of use
themes.summary: Users in this cluster are overwhelmingly praising Netflix for its wide selection of movies, series, and documentaries, along with smooth streaming quality and an easy-to-navigate interface. Several mention personalized recommendations, offline downloads, and cross-device continuity as reasons they keep using the app. The only request-like comment is a single review noting occasional problems and issues, but it gives no detail.
themes.recommendation: Protect the current discovery and streaming experience in regression testing for Android releases, and add a short in-app feedback prompt that captures what the occasional problems were so the team can follow up on that vague complaint.

themes.label: Foreign-language content lacks language filtering
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS say Netflix's recommendations and Home screen push dubbed or foreign-language titles, and they want a way to filter by audio language or see the language before pressing play. Several report wasted time starting a title only to find it has no English audio or subtitles, and some say the dub-versus-subtitle mismatch on specific shows and devices makes viewing frustrating. Many ask for a separate foreign-language category or language labels in descriptions.
themes.recommendation: Scope a product spike on an audio-language filter and a visible language label on title tiles and detail pages, starting with a mockup test for a 'Foreign Language' browse row and an option to exclude titles without English audio or subtitles from recommendations.

themes.label: Requests for more seasons
themes.summary: This cluster mixes praise for story, characters, and performances with requests for more content. Many users ask for season 2 or renewal after a show was cancelled or ended on a cliffhanger, including Julie and the Phantoms, Stranger Things, Old Money, and Miraculous. Others ask for titles to be restored or added, such as Hotel Transylvania, the Barbie films, and full Winx Club seasons, and a few complain about cuts or content they find objectionable.
themes.recommendation: Tag reviews in this cluster by title and request type (renewal, restoration, licensing, content concerns), then send the top titles with the most renewal requests to the content and licensing teams with a short report on demand volume and sentiment.

reviews.t: My favorite streaming app! A few things to fix though
reviews.x: Okay so first off I just want to say that Netflix is probably the best streaming app to get, especially for families. I appreciate the rating systems and the kids settings and also love the variety of shows and movies to watch on there. I like the layout, though sometimes there are differences between tvs, iPads, and phones. This is overall a great app to use if you get annoyed with ads (though keep in mind for live events, at least in my experience, there are many ads) To address some things that aren’t my favorite or could improve-I know it’s not always possible, but sometimes it can be frustrating when only certain seasons or episodes are on the app, meaning if you want to see the other seasons, you’ll either just have to deal with it or watch it somewhere else. Next, sometimes, especially with older shows, it will say pg or y-7 but will contain some inappropriate stuff. Not extreme but if a child has a kids account, it’s probably not exactly what a parent would want their kids watching/listening to (ex. Seinfeld). And finally, this is a big ask, but an option for parents to choose certain shows and movies their kids can watch from certain ratings instead of having to go through and block a bunch of shows when they change the rating allowed. (Sorry if that doesn’t make sense but here’s the example-a tween/teen has a kids account up to pg but wants to watch some movies or tv shows that are pg13/tv14. Changing the rating to this would allow the child to have a chance at seeing or hearing something inappropriate. And going through and picking certain shows/movies is not only time consuming, but also doesn’t really affect the problem bc there is a limit to how much you can block. So instead, allowing certain movies or shows the parent knows is safe for their kid to watch would be a lot more effective and convenient without having to completely change the ratings allowed.) TLDR-Great streaming app if you want no ads, an upgrade would be being able to choose certain shows from higher ratings for your kids to watch without changing the entire account rating. Sorry for the long review, if you read this, then thank you!

reviews.t: Netflix’s Household Wi-Fi Policy Is Unfair to College Students
reviews.x: As a college student, I absolutely despise Netflix’s “household Wi-Fi” feature. Just because I live in a dorm and use a different Wi-Fi network than my family does not mean I should constantly be getting logged out of an account I’m already paying for or have permission to use. College students go away to school, live on campus, and travel, so why are we being punished for simply living somewhere other than our family’s house? It’s extremely frustrating to have to keep dealing with verification and getting kicked off just because I’m connected to my dorm’s Wi-Fi instead of my household’s. Netflix should make this a CHOICE. Give account owners the option to decide whether devices should be logged out when they connect to a different Wi-Fi network instead of automatically enforcing this feature on everyone. Not everyone is sharing their account with strangers; some of us are literally college students trying to watch Netflix while away at school. This policy is unfair, inconvenient, and honestly makes me want to cancel my subscription. Netflix needs to consider students and families who live in different places instead of making the viewing experience unnecessarily difficult.

reviews.t: Stop Discriminating and Appropriating my Religious Identity
reviews.x: Netflix has been turning a blind eye against discrimination, appropriation, religious mockery, and blatant double standards. If “representation matters,” then that principle does not disappear when the identity being represented is Christian. My faith is not an aesthetic. My religion is not a costume. Christian stories like Narnia are not empty cultural property to be stripped of their meaning, repackaged, and sold back to audiences while the people who actually hold those beliefs are told to stop being so sensitive. You cannot demand respect for culture, heritage, identity, and lived experience everywhere else, then treat religious conviction as uniquely disposable. And that is exactly why Netflix’s handling of Narnia matters. The Chronicles of Narnia is not merely a fantasy franchise with a few Christian references sprinkled on top. Its Christian imagination is woven into its moral architecture, symbolism, themes of sacrifice, redemption, resurrection, kingship, and grace. If Netflix wants the cultural capital of Narnia, it should also be prepared to respect the convictions embedded in the work by CS Lewis rather than treating them as inconvenient material to be diluted or rewritten. Either appropriation and erasure are real concerns, or they are slogans applied selectively. Netflix is free to produce whatever it wants. I am equally free to stop financing a morally bankrupt company whose stated values seem to end where it starts becoming inconvenient for them. Subscription cancelled. App deleted.

Perfect for relaxing after a busy day! ❤️🍿

Netflix still gives you an incredible amount of value for the money. Even at around $25–$30 a month, I think you’re getting more than your money’s worth. A night at the movie theater for two people can easily cost that much or more, and that’s for just one movie. With Netflix, you get access to a huge selection of movies, documentaries, international films, independent and indie films, original productions, and TV series whenever you want. I’ve discovered plenty of movies on Netflix that I probably never would have seen anywhere else. I honestly think some of the complaints about the Netflix catalog are a little ridiculous. No streaming service is going to have every movie ever made or the entire world’s catalog. People sometimes expect Netflix to have everything while also being better than HBO, Disney+, Prime Video, and every other streaming service combined. That’s simply unrealistic. Netflix also deserves a lot of credit for helping pioneer the streaming era. Long before every major studio had its own streaming service, Netflix helped change the way we watch movies and television at home. For the variety, convenience, original content, indie films, international movies, and the amount of entertainment you can get out of one subscription, I still think Netflix is one of the best values in streaming.

Now it pauses and brings up the frame selector, and then you have to click again. Did they not do any research or usability testing before releasing this? It's also not smooth at all. There are multiple other features of the tvOS player that are now unavailable in the Netflix app including the handy auto-subtitling that kicks in when you rewind or mute the show; the option to use Enhance Dialog; the info and video/audio format details in the slide-up menu, the ability to double-tap and find out when the show or movie ends, and even integration with the useful 'Remote' app on iPhone and iPad. Already Netflix not integrating with TV app for up next and continue watching itself a big disappointing user experience. With the latest changes I get the feel of why to continue with the subscription to go through these kind of user experience ordeals on top of there ever hiking subscription costs!

reviews.t: Too expensive for all the issues!!
reviews.x: I have been a loyal customer of Netflix ever since Netflix was a company that you could order DVDs from. It has become increasingly more expensive (it’s gotten ridiculously more expensive) and now I can’t even use it upstairs and downstairs in my home because my home requires that we have an internet router for each story because the wireless signal doesn’t reach downstairs if it’s placed upstairs and vice versa. It’s an issue that we have tried 1 million different ways to correct for the past seven years and this is the only resolution we have found. Because of the dual routers, Netflix views the two different routers as two different households, even though it’s in the same house and therefore we cannot use the account that I’m paying this increasingly climbing amount of money for in two different rooms in my same house. That is absolutely absurd. And the main reason for this is because they don’t want people sharing Netflix accounts! That is absolutely insane to me. This now enormous corporation is really so worried about how we choose to use the account that we pay for that we can’t even use the account in our same home if we have two different Internet routers. And it freezes and has issues! This infuriates me to the point of canceling!

So far, Netflix has released ONE EPISODE of a 30+ episode anime and dropped a trailer for the SECOND EPISODE and said it would release sometime this year. That could very easily mean we are stuck waiting for 8 months with now two episodes to show for it. Netflix is doing everything in their power to ruin all the hype around the show. I did not think it could get worse than part 6, where Netflix made viewers wait over half a year for 1/3 of the season, but Netflix has truly outdone themselves by lowering the bar even further! Instead of having to wait roughly 8 months for 12 episodes… now us millions of viewers get the privilege of waiting months to years for singular episodes. Netflix needs to sell the rights to Jojos because they are doing the worst possible job at adapting the manga into an anime in a timely and quality manner.

Netflix has been a household name for YEARS now. As someone born in the 2000s, a lot of early childhood memories came from netflix's original business model of movie and show rental. When Netflix switched over to the streaming model we all know and despise, people praised them for providing a viable and cheaper option to cable television. For years netflix stood almost uncontested as the best in class for entertainment among younger people. Once they started to BE contested, however, they've made some of the most abhorrent and terrible business decisions I can think of. Whether it be delisting their original projects, writing their shows into a hole, cancelling projects that people loved, pushing shows that people hate, or the infamous nearly quarterly price hikes. Netflix, in their goal to expand their list of media and replace at-home entertainment, has completely lost the plot as to why they were so successful in the first place; providing a cheaper but smaller catalogue of quality content, wherever you choose to watch it. I really hope they re-evaluate their business model and listen to consumer feedback soon. Also, release steel ball run

The only way to skip back while you are watching a movie now involves you having to skim through a menu of pictures of scenes from the movie. That invariably causes you to have to skip back more than 30 seconds now. Gone are the days where you could just skip back 10 seconds to repeat a piece of dialogue that you may not have understood. This change is a perfect example of completely unnecessarily “improving” something in an pp simply to make a change no one ever requested. On a 4K television the new controls are so huge, it makes you wonder if the app developers are hard of seeing. So not only do we lose the skip back function, we have to deal with a huge and ugly playback menu as well. What a terrible change that affects the #1 reason we use this app: to playback movies.

I write this review just before uninstalling and leaving Netflix. I have been a subscriber since 2013, and content and psychological/emotional safety of content has deteriorated beyond repair. Recommendations are inappropriate and often toxic and outright painful. The algorithm vacillates between offering two extremes of content, both absolutely inappropriate for me, because I don't fit into their narrow demographic models. This intensified after turning 50, like a ledge, and it also has a lot of problems with gender stereotyping demographic parameters. The result is that I keep going back to see if there is anything watchable, and can't find a thing, and sometimes get distressed by the content it decides to offer... and nothing gets viewed. And the decent stuff, the old standby staples, keep getting removed and presented exclusively on other premium streaming services. After a few years of logging in, spinning around for hours and not finding anything but upsetting or otherwise inappropriate (for me) content, I'm done with this. I've discovered the joys of outright purchasing the things I love directly from Apple so they're always available, and watch for it on sale, so in the end, it's much more cost effective than subscribing to Netflix and not watching a thing.

reviews.t: Frustration With Netflix Household Policy Blocking Legitimate Users
reviews.x: I am extremely frustrated and disappointed with the recent changes to Netflix’s account and household policies. My family pays for this account and each of us has our own profile. However, I am now being blocked with a message saying that my device is not part of the “Netflix household.” This policy feels unfair and frustrating for legitimate users who are part of a paid account. Real families do not always live under the exact same roof, and these restrictions end up punishing customers who are already paying for the service. Changes like this do not improve the user experience. Instead, they create frustration, disappointment, and make many of us seriously consider canceling the account. If Netflix continues moving in this direction, the service loses much of the value that made people subscribe in the first place. I hope Netflix reconsiders these policies or provides a fairer and more flexible solution for families who share accounts. Otherwise, the most reasonable option will be to cancel the account and look for other entertainment platforms.

reviews.t: DO NOT GET RID OF SHE-RA AND THE PRINCESSES OF POWER
reviews.x: DO NOT GET RID OF SHE-RA AND THE PRINCESSES OF POWER How about instead of features that prevent you from casting when you're not on your home network, Netflix becomes more diligent about content warnings when titles reflect potentially triggering scenes and themes? Given, "mature audiences" is an extremely vague rating. While the majority of "mature watchers" may have no issue with all things presented, others may enjoy mature content with a desire to avoid select themes so that they may actually enjoy what they are watching. On another note, their capitalistic and greedy changes to Wi-Fi and account settings on family accounts was blatantly greedy. I don't think I am alone in hoping a more benevolent company takes them over to retain its redeeming features, such as content and the availability to download, and bring back it's former glory. Besides that, why on earth was introducing games into a streaming app thought actually relevant or a good idea? But you know what has really been a problem from the start and continues to be unreliable; how they categorize genres. Gross DO NOT GET RID OF SHE-RA AND THE PRINCESSES OF POWER

I’ve been using Netflix for years, and the subscription prices going up with inflation and whatnot is one thing, but there are so many other unnecessary things that have been changed. First of all, priding yourselves on being an ad free streaming service only to make the “normal” priced plan now include ads, only for them to be removed with an even more expensive plan is wild. Second, starting the household idea which kicked thousands of people off of their family accounts?? I say this as a college student who is sharing an account with my parents, which leads to the main reason I wanted to write this review: I just got kicked off of my computer of all things for not being in the household… while I’m currently visiting my parents at the main household for the account. It makes no sense, and regardless of location, it feels very greedy to not even allow us to watch on mobile devices anymore when the main people doing so seem to be college students. After creating all of these new features that make it more and more difficult to continue using the service, Netflix has also become notorious for cancelling popular shows and movies, as well as removing others. I find myself having trouble finding things to watch at times due to how many things are being removed… it makes me wonder how much longer it’ll really be worth it to continue paying for a subscription, honestly. All in all, Netflix really needs to do better because as of right now, it feels like they couldn’t care less about the consumers which in turn makes me feel less like I should continue using their services.

Thank God for "FRANKENSTEIN" because I was beginning to think going to the cinema is a waste of my time. Writer and director Guillermo Del Toro tells a story, that starts slowly but builds to a compelling climax. Del Toro is responsible for the classic "Pan's Labyrinth" and his Oscar winning "The Shape Of Water" where he intertwines horror, terrific cinematography, superb art direction, and takes audiences for a fantasy ride. Oscar Isaac is Victor Frankenstein, a scientist, who believes that he can defy death and create a live being from corpses. The creature he creates is played by Jacob Elordi. The first part is narrated by Isaac and we get to understand his motives. The second part is narrated by Elordi and we get to understand how he adjusts to living without being human, and not dying. The moral is "be careful what you wish for” and "no man should feel that he's God"; Frankenstein is a narcissist like our "current president who wants to be a King." Isaac has his best role in his lengthy career. Elordi discards his handsome boy image playing the creature. We have seen movies about Frankenstein before but never with such detail. Del Toro will probably be Oscar nominated for his excellent direction. Most impressive are the art direction, visual effects, and cinematography. I'm glad that I saw it on the big screen and I did not wait for Netflix (distributor). The images from the movie are unforgettable and will remain with me for a while.

reviews.t: A Request for Smarter Netflix Sharing Options
reviews.x: I’ve been a huge Netflix fan since the days when they were just a DVD-by-mail service. I love Netflix, and honestly, I’m the reason my parents still keep their subscription - without me, they probably would’ve canceled by now. One big issue, though, is the rule that everyone must be in the same household or on the same WiFi to stay on one account. Just today, I got kicked out of Netflix on my phone because I wasn’t on the home WiFi. That doesn’t make sense to me. I should be able to watch anything, anywhere, on my phone with a service my family is paying for. My brother is a college student who can’t afford his own Netflix account, so it would be great if he could keep using the family account like he always has. That seems fair, right? Maybe Netflix could charge a small extra fee for each out-of-household member. That would be a smarter, more flexible way to handle things. Netflix, please consider this!

reviews.t: So many different options to watch
reviews.x: I love Netflix because of the range of different content you can watch. Whether it be KDramas, anime, crime, documentaries, shows with LGBTQ characters, you name it. Speaking of which and first of all, Netflix is not pushing or forcing shows with LGBTQ characters onto anyone. They are called options for a reason. These kinds of shows are just a handful among thousands of other different options. If you do not like these kinds of shows, then that’s fine. Don’t watch them and watch something else on Netflix. If you are a parent and you do not want your child or children to watch shows with LGBTQ characters, then that’s fine. Monitor what your children watch. It’s called being a parent. Second, you shouldn’t call for the removal of a show or movie just because you don’t like it. While you dislike it, there are countless others who do, so Netflix should not deprive the rights of others to watch something that offends you over its existence. Finally, two of the biggest downsides to Netflix are the crackdown on password sharing and the delayed effect on some captions in foreign films and shows.

Ohhh Netflix. I used to love you so much, but it turns out... I've actually just been in love with the idea of you :( First, you banned password sharing... AKA the only reason half of us even had Netflix in the first place. Remember that cute little tweet you made?? What was it.... "Love is sharing a password." Mhmmm. And don’t give me the ‘household only’ excuse, either. My sister is literally away at college. She is still part of my family, she still comes home for breaks, and she’s still on our account. But apparently, unless she’s watching from the living room couch, she has to cough up her own subscription? Make it make sense. Let's also bring up how you’ve ruined streaming. Back in the cable days, I was loyal. I was on my couch at the same time every week, excited for the next episode. Now? You dangle a season over our heads, make us wait more than a year for the next one, and by the time it drops, I’ve forgotten half the plot and stopped caring. Honestly, cable beat you here - at least they respected consistency. And pleeeaseee do not get me started on Netflix Originals. For every decent one, there are about 10 with acting so bad I genuinely sit there wondering if I'm being punk'd. Why am I paying premium prices to cringe-watch something that feels like it was shot in a middle school drama club? Oh, and the movie shuffle? A film will be here for a few months, then vanish to another platform, then another. Why? So I have to subscribe to five different services just to finish the movie I started? Congratulations. You’ve turned ‘cord-cutting’ into ‘wallet-draining.’ Every rich company gets richer while the rest of us get nickel-and-dimed to death. At this rate, people will cancel faster than you can greenlight another ‘true crime docuseries that probably doesn't need to be a series in the first place’. Stop testing how far you can push us before we remember books exist :)

netflix overall is an amazing app if you would like to watch movies, or tv shows ad-free. i’ve grown up with this platform and i’ve bonded over it. however, i’ve come across a few problems that i believe should be addressed. for one, they remove or cancel all popular shows and replace them with corny teen shows, or just kid shows. don’t get me wrong, they are great for that specific target audience, but half of the good shows are gone. what really annoys basically everyone is that a show could have 3 seasons but they only put 1-2. not all shows are like this though, so don’t expect the worst. i believe letting us choose which shows we want back and replace it with one of the shows they added would be a better choice and that would make most of us happier. another bad part is that they made an update where you have to be part of the household the account was made from. this account was made by a family member of mine that i’ve been using since. but they moved away and i can’t watch netflix anymore. we have tried multiple times to make us to try and be part of the household. it would work for maybe 5 days, and then it wouldn’t again. this problem annoys me the most. take my words with a grain of salt though. this is a great movie/show watching platform and i genuinely do love it. but these needs to be fixed.

reviews.t: Hate the recent Netflix app updates
reviews.x: Simply put in three words “endless side scrolling”. I’m not sure what it is about app developers, in particular streaming app developers who are under the impression that endless side scrolling is a great thing. When I click on “my list” I want a horizontal view of my list like it used to show. I don’t want previews playing at every stop on the list. Now while watching the tv app, I have to keep my tablet at hand just to be able to see a horizontal view of my list. If Netflix’s goal was to present its customers with information overload via this new user interface, then I guess they have succeeded. They used to have the best user interface. Instead of being innovative they simply copied every other pay streaming service’s interface and they executed it in the worst possible way. Apple TV used to have the worst UI, but now Netflix has won that first prize. If finding what I want to watch is this hard Netflix, then your service isn’t worth the money you charge.

This documentary is a must watch. I was walking out of tower I when the first plane hit. I remember watching tower II crumble right in front of me as I stood there too shocked to start running from the smoke and debris as they snaked through the streets of lower Manhattan. This series captures the spirit of those moments in ways that you can only understand if you were there. More importantly this production touches on how this one event (that changed all of our lives) was really the commutation of a series of events. It speaks to how in our efforts to avenge this horrific event we may have lost our way as a country. I appreciate that the series highlighted a time (a moment, one of many moments) when America truly was great. A time where we came together without the prompting of political operatives and without regard to whether you wear the red or the blue jersey to celebrate our shared accomplishment.

I almost never watch television so I don’t really need Netflix or any other streaming platforms, however I felt as though Netflix was just one of those streaming platforms everyone just had. However into their slow decent into becoming…. Worse.. it feels as though the shows or movies I want to watch are never on here even though it says it is when I look up where to watch ____. I rated it 5-stars because it was the easiest subscription cancelation I’ve ever gone through. Most companies that require a monthly subscription often hide where to cancel or won’t even allow you to do it online, on top of that before you hit cancel for most places it begs you to stay, offering lower prices and promises to be better. I find that absolutely pathetic and annoying every time. If I’m canceling my monthly subscription one month of it being $5 cheaper isn’t going to change my mind, if they really cared they would’ve offered the lower price from the jump. Not Netflix, you hit cancel, then one more time to confirm, and that’s it. No lower prices, no begging, nothing… If I’m being honest it was relieving to not have to go through an annoying process that inevitably strengthens my disdain for the service I am canceling which in return makes me never want to come back because I know it’s a major pain to cancel when I don’t want it. Netflix will always be a service I come back to when I need to watch something and I appreciate them sticking strong to pricing and understanding that someone canceling their service doesn’t mean they’ll never come back, just that it’s not needed at this time. Thank you Netflix.

Netflix and the whole streaming industry have bamboozled everyone one. We supposedly paid for commercial free on demand streaming of entire movie series or television series. We were paying for the convenience of watching what we wanted when we wanted without interruption or scheduling. Now fast forward some years… Now we wait a whole off season if not a whole year or longer to watch a new series or a series of movies! To make matters worse you don’t even get to binge watch a series anymore you have to wait for the same time next week for the next episode. Sound familiar? Also no commercials interruption was what we paid for yet now we get commercials before after and sometimes even during the program. Sound familiar? Commercial advertising is how public broadcasting services make money. We were tired of the constant interruption so we were willing to pay for cable then eventually streaming services to avoid all the advertising and waiting weeks to see what’s next on your favorite show. If everything I’m communicating sounds familiar it is because it was called free television. Somehow streaming giants like Netflix have tricked us while consistently raising prices to the point where it is the same cost of cable with less content and no live broadcast, into paying for free television while doubling dipping by selling advertising on top of charging us subscription fees. Wow!

A sensitive exploration of the human heart, and the dynamics of relationships. The shaping of personalities, and the developments of men and women in relationships are more and more evident, with actions and responses building throughout the movie. The plot reveals that close family relationships, friendships, sexual desire, .and romance can easily blurr our perceptions, then sometimes quickly make sharp turns with insecurity, jealousy, that can then lead to violence. Domestic violence is explored in relationships, that seems pushed aside earlier in the movie, with some clues, but the raw truth becomes more evident in the end and leads to a grounded closure. The buildings, names of characters, scenes, costumes. backdrops, businesses, parks, trees, flower shop, and vitality of Boston, with brilliant acting by all the central personalities, adds to the rich and bold development of such memorable, likeable characters. Great background songs and musical arrangements adds to the story line.

reviews.t: A fun family action pack movie that delivers!
reviews.x: I just watched back in action with my family and we loved it. This was a great example of a family, friendly film that is suitable for children and adults alike. The storyline is engaging and the action scenes are thrilling and the cast is diverse and talented. One of the things that stayed out for me was a positive representation of in interracial couples in the main characters. It’s refreshing to see a movie that celebrates diversity and inclusivity, and it’s something I think it’s important for families to see. But what really made this movie shine was the way the entire family was involved in the action it was a great way to see the parents and children working together, using their unique skills and strength to overcome obstacles and save the day. The chemistry between the cast members was palpable. And it was clear that they all had a blast making this movie overall, I highly recommend back in action to families who were looking for a fun entertaining movie that is suitable for all ages. It’s a great way to spend quality time together and it’s a movie that will leave you feeling uplifted and inspired so grab some popcorn gathered a family and get ready to enjoy this movie with a wild ride.

Recently tried to cast from my phone to Chromecast to watch Delicious and found out that the ads tier doesn’t support casting. ARE YOU KIDDING ME? I can deal with ads vs no-ads tiers as far as payment plans, sure, but to completely remove features that are standard on EVERY SINGLE OTHER SERVICE, most of which are CHEAPER, is insane. This wasn’t the only reason I’m irritated, obviously Netflix hates their users with all the issues with account sharing and tiers, but it’s the final straw. I will find other streaming services - like the bundle for Disney+/Hulu for much better pricing and service than Netflix - and I will not be returning to Netflix again unless changes are made. Will be encouraging my friends to do the same.

My mother was in the 6888. My brothers and I knew she was in the army in WWII and drove trucks and knew drivers in the red ball express and that’s it. Now I see why we had inspections on Saturday mornings, spit shining our shoes and organizing our foot lockers and clothes in order. My dad was in the army from WWII through viet nam. I now have a much better understanding of my parents and why they were so tough and taught us no task is impossible. Sometimes it takes courage and belief. We had it when we integrated schools and everyone in our neighborhood wanted their kids in her kindergarten class. The movie could have been a mini series and characters fleshed out more . The fighter pilot could have been a Tuskegee flyer as they were based at Ramiteli Italy. However, seeing them march brought tears to my eyes. America has under appreciated the contributions of Black American women. It’s a shame my mom did not see this movie. At least I was able to get her full military honors for her burial. After seeing the trailers i thought this would be Tyler Perry’s best work. I’m glad I ignored the naysayers and critics. This is one of the most educational things i have ever seen from Hollywood and I have seen a lot. God bless Tyler Perry and the cast and crew.

reviews.t: Decreased quality service with increased subscription fees and ads
reviews.x: I have used Netflix for most of my adult life, dating back to the time of mail-in DVDs. Up until the last two years, it was still the go-to streaming service to watch and download shows for those on the go. Even with a couple of price hikes, Netflix was still a great streaming service. That’s why I found it shocking that Netflix has now limited the number MONTHLY downloads to 15 when in fact it used to be unlimited. In my line of work, WiFi has not always been readily available. There could be multiple months where the internet wasn’t available, which made port stops vital for downloading new shows to prepare long upcoming underway periods. Netflix has now gone the way of Prime and NFL streaming services in the sense that they pump ads into their shows and removed once available features and placed them into more expensive subscription packages. Even with the upgraded package, the number of monthly downloads is 100 per month. The quality of this service, similar to others, has diminished. It’s sad to say, but Netflix and the other streaming services have become the modern day cable tv with added commercials and increased price tags. With life becoming more expensive, my family will likely say goodbye to this streaming service.

reviews.t: Disappointed with what Netflix has become
reviews.x: For the record, I am not someone who writes reviews lightly. I have been an avid Netflix watcher for over ten years. With time, I have watched the platform get worse while simultaneously becoming greedier. Netflix has functionally turned its back on everything that initially drew people to the platform. They used to be affordably priced with a wide selection of shows. They have steadily jacked up the price during a pandemic and cost of living crisis in an effort to capitalize on one of the few affordable methods of entertainment left. The variety of show options has decreased. They used to have no ads, as an alternative to cable television. They now have ads if you don’t want to pay their ridiculous prices. Now they say they won’t let families share accounts when they don’t live in the same household. How greedy can these people get? What about college students, split family households, military families, or people who travel for work? I recently learned that I can’t even cast the show on my phone to the TV without upgrading my account. My blood is boiling and I am sick of the corporate money grabs. Do better Netflix.

I’d like to simply report some technical bugs I have been experiencing over the course of a year now, they aren’t major and there are work arounds which is why I haven’t said anything. Firstly, when binge watching a show, the little “skip intro” “next episode” “skip recap” stop working properly. I’ll reach the end of an episode, and when I use the “next episode” prompt, it gets stuck in a loading screen mode and nothing will happen. I left it like that to see how long it would take and my TV went to sleep from how long it was left on….. The work around is physically going to the bottom and clicking on the next episode. Something new though, I’m watching Dexter and your Netflix and chills: It’s Halloween! video randomly begins playing in the background. So as I watch any show or movie on your platform, the audio to that video “preview” in the background randomly…. The work around is closing the app and restarting. Not very fun. reviews.t: Probably spent more years on Netflix than my entire life
reviews.x: Guys I have to beg my mummy every week not to get rid of Netflix 😕😕😕 Okay genuinely, I have been watching Netflix since I was a kid. Netflix has always been my number one app if we are being honest. Nowadays, im not a kid anymore. I watch more anime related stuff. (Not one of those weirdos.) and like I’ve been mad and heart broken because Netflix has removed so many anime’s that were so good. Especially ones that got me into anime. (Silent voice, toradora, the promised never land for example.) now I understand that they have contracts and if these shows aren’t working out it’s in their best interest to remove them. I understand the company wants money, but I wish they would keep some of the shows. They may not be popular but they mean a lot to the people who do watch them. Now I originally planned to yap about this like months ago, but I didn’t feel like it because literally, what’s there for someone like me to say about it? And then I find out they are removed the untamed. Now listen, I started watching that because it was based off a novel my friend read. Those were like 44 mins each and 50 episodes. I finished it in a week, in between school hours and all that. This show literally gave me some purpose in that week. Once I finished it, I felt empty. It was this show that started me collecting actual novels. Now I know I’m being dramatic here, and I can obviously rewatch it on other apps and websites, but I’m sick and tired of Netflix removing all the shows that hold meaning to me 🙁🙁🙁 I still love you Netflix, just heart broken 💔

I’ve been watching Netflix for as long as I can remember. I’ve had a Netflix account for as long as I’ve had money to spend on Netflix and before that, I lived with my family and used theirs. I like to watch on mobile and I’m a passive watcher so I use picture-in-picture. I’m also single and I live alone, so I have the simplest plan. I got an email about a month ago, letting me know that they were giving me reduced price on my plan. They framed this as a good thing for me. However, I soon learned that this reduced plan would come with ads. A bit misleading, but fine. Whatever. I’ll deal with the ads because I’m not going to be tricked into paying more money just to rewatch a show that I’ve already seen 20 times. Well unbeknownst to me, they also quietly removed the picture-in-picture feature from the standard plan with ads. This is where I draw the line. This is a basic feature. To have it held hostage in exchange for paying double the price that was advertised to me is ridiculous. I am cancelling my membership and I have no plans to return, as I am being billed annually at a reasonable price by a competitor.

reviews.t: Chill, Eat, Relax, and just Take a Break.
reviews.x: Dear Netflix (or to the people who own it), this is a very good app all though, i understand why you guys have added adds but people are saying they are getting them a little too much. I’m not aging get rid of them, i’m just saying maybe a little less, I honestly haven’t gotten THAT many, but there is times where i get annoyed by them. But I mean, who doesn’t?🤨 Another thing I want to say is please please please stop removing the good movies and shows.😭 I understand you have to remove movies at one point but why can’t you remove the less popular, and not as good movies/shows because i hate having to go on all kinds of different apps to find the good movies that i want to watch. Other than all this, Netflix is one of my favorite apps to watch things on. A lot of my fav shows/movies are free on here which i’m very happy about, and it’s a very nice app. To all the people questioning getting it, i recommend you do. it’s a very nice site to go on, watch your favorite movie, chill and take a break from school/work stress, and don’t blame me if you get hooked! (cuz i am too😭)

reviews.t: App stopped working AFTER Netflix enabled ads
reviews.x: Netflix app stopped working on my older iPad running iOS 12.5.7 on Sept 6, 2024 after Netflix enabled ads on my subscription plan. Their “Standard with ads” plan is $6.99/month. When I reached out to Netflix on Sept 7th, I was told a ticket would be opened with their developers to have their “Download an older version of this app” to work as it previously did with the AD FREE version. I told her my iPad worked fine with ads on the PRIME VIDEO app. I was also told I would receive an email with the ticket information…..I called back on Sunday, Sept 8, 2024 requesting escalation to a Supervisor because no ticket had been created for the issue and no email had been sent to me - I had been LIED to…..Supervisor stated ADS ONLY WORK with iOS 15 & later. I advised her I would NOT be forced (bullied/strong-armed) into paying MORE MONEY for an app that stopped working because they would not make a simple configuration change. I primarily watch Netflix using my iPad so I requested immediate cancellation of the subscription. I know they do not care that they lost a long time customer because they have so many new customers.

reviews.t: Annoying Product Error Message Let’s Your Customers Down
reviews.x: After downloading content for a plane trip across the states, I pulled up Emily in Paris and started watching it. I had to pause the show for a sec and open another window to look at something else on my iPad. When I came back to watch the show 5 mins later, the download tile said “Expires in 48h”. That’s fine. But when I clicked on the episode to continue watching it - again after just 5 minutes of being away from the episode, I got the message “Error. This title can no longer be watched offline.” And I now cannot watch the show for the remainder of the flight. What the heck? I’ve been forgiving little quirks here and there that have been popping up a lot recently, but this error (or actual purposeful product change?) was the tipping point for me to finally write a review. With continued price increases, I expect your product quality to go up, not down. Please fix this product issue. Currently, you’re really letting this customer down.

I can’t believe how hard they’re cracking down on accounts “outside of the owner household” my family is split up just like 50-60% of families in the US. We share a Netflix account. Just enough for my parents, sister, and I. Everything has been fine with that and all of us trying to live okay on our own until now, each pitching in to the “family account”. I work hard enough as it is to pay for the essentials in life like rent, groceries, utilities, gas, car repairs, basic clothing, etc. I hardly have enough money to eat out nowadays at Panera or Qdoba or anything slightly better than McDonald’s and I work 40 hours a week. I can’t even think of starting a family. I can’t imagine feeding more mouths than mine and my girlfriend. Inflation has made living in 2024 unbearable for the middle class. Saving for vacations of any sort is a joke when I still have to pay off student loans. All I want to do is have a little entertainment at the end of my work day. My moral and outlook for the future has never felt so bleak. I can barely rap my head around the greed surrounding the decisions to make these menial products more expensive. There’s just no way to justify these changes rationally. Everything was fine and Netflix was still making billions but they just keep wanting more and more while the common man rots. I will never use Netflix again or any service associated with them unless something changes for the better and they actually show some humility to the people that got them to where they are now. I hope I’m not the only person that thinks this way and these huge companies start to feel the sting of the public waking up and becoming sick if the blind idiotic greed that’s consuming our nation. You guys could learn a thing or two from Arizona iced tea and why I’ll be a customer of theirs for the rest of my life and why I’ll condemn you until we see change.

I’ll get to the point. I understand Netflix doesn’t want those pepes using vpns to watch whatever show they want but what about actual travelers. This has been a major nuisance for the past fue years. Basically, when your location changes (like going to another country) the content changes as well and it varies. Some things you saw before are gone but some things you didn’t see are there. People try taking advantage of this by using a vpn to make it look like they’re in another country to watch content that isn’t available in their country. But Netflix has a “fix”. They simply set the language specifically to whatever languages are spoken in that country. But then this conflicts with people that are ACTUALLY on vacation. I’ve had to watch mha in Spanish. Luckily I know Spanish but i don’t know French. I don’t know German. I don’t know Japanese. I watched season 1 of Mob Psycho 100 on the way to Switzerland and made the mistake of not downloading season 2. So now I have the options of watching it in Japanese or German. And no, no english subtitles either. There is not a SINGLE show of my interest in my language. So now Netflix, my main entertainment on the plane for example, is utterly useless. Absolutely useless. Now I have to watch the Acolyte and who knows what else on Disney+ for a 9 hour flight.

I’ve been a loyal customer to for 5+ years without ever taking a break from the subscription. However as my family has grown we’ve also spread farther apart and don’t see each other as often. Netflix is one of the few ways we can connect with each other from time to time. Not to mention the cost of living has gone up which means it’s harder to pay for subscriptions especially when the price of the subscription goes up just about every year. The thing is you’re not the only tv service that i can subscribe to that will actually think about the consumer as a human being and not just someone they can pull money from. Ever since the new “household” update why whole family has been thinking canceling our netflix account. Since not only is the price always rising but also the freedom that came with using the account. I find it unacceptable that you get to raise the price AND dictate how our account is used when several other services that I could subscribe too that are affordable, give discounts, provide quality show and movies, and allow their customers to enjoy the account that they paid for without any type of bothersome restrictions. Now I do understand making sure the amount of screens being used at the same time is limited but that should be the only one. If you have to add that many restrictions to your customers then the content is the problem NOT the customer. Let me clarify if you didn’t understand YOU are the issue for YOURSELF. I hope that you do look into fixing this issue because you do have a few good shows and i’m on the verge of canceling my account. Have a great rest of your day!

reviews.t: Netflix is great, just a few recommendations
reviews.x: I have loved Netflix for a long time and it has easy access to my favorite shows and movies. It is definitely one of the better TV apps. One thing I recommend is adding more languages. I've been trying to learn Portuguese for a while and someone gave me the great idea to use subtitles but when I went to my favorite TV show, there weren't any Portuguese subtitles along with a lot of other languages I didn't suspect would not have been there. It might help a lot of avid Netflix binge watchers to learn a language if they had accessibility to that language in subtitles. Another recommendation is that people love a lot of the TV shows and movies Netflix gets rid of. My favorite movies/TV shows have gotten the best seasons taken away, or the entirety of it taken away. My little brothers just loved a little kids TV show, but Netflix took away all the seasons except for the first, which had the most boring episodes in it. So please take into consideration my recommendations, this could improve a lot of peoples watching experiences.

I’ve had Netflix since 2014 and I’ve never had a bad movie or series experience, but I do have a problem with some of the series and movies they take off/on, and how long they take them off for, like when it comes to series that I love like “The Vampire Diaries” and “The Originals”. I understand they have to take some series off so they can put new ones or the ones they took off before that one back on, but how long some of the series are gone is crazy it has now almost been a whole year since “The Vampire Diaries” has been off of Netflix and I am a binge watcher so I love to rewatch series and movies that I love, but a year is toooo long for me, I like to get my binge watching on and Netflix is lowkey stopping me from that, and DON’T GET ME STARTED ON THE MOVIES, I am a fantasy, romance, drama, comedy girl, so I love movies like twilight and I do now for sure that Netflix takes that movie on and off all the time, but once again the amount of time that it gets taken off for is crazy. Me personally I think Netflix should take series on and off based off what is actually being watched by people, and if they take a series or movie off, and it’s a movie/series that people have been watching a lot they should take it off for a short amount of time (3-5 months)

reviews.t: So sad/mad, they ruined it for me.
reviews.x: I. LOVE. Netflix. I watch it often and the best part is they don’t currently have ads on the shows even thought Prime and Disney do, even though I still pay for the apps so I Don’t constantly have to watch ads. Today, I opened up my phone and wanted to watch the new Avatar: the Last Air Bender on Netflix since both of my tv’s are currently in use. It was offloaded and can’t reinstall. Why? Because three days ago they made an update requiring the IOS 16 or later software update. I own an iPhone 7. I can no longer watch my glorious Netflix. The sad part is it didn’t even really need an update. They just did it because they hadn’t updated in a while. 😭 Only other complaints are: 1. They take away movies/shows just to make me mad. If they do add them back, they only have them for a limited amount of time if they do add them again. Very few do they keep permanently. Or at least a few years. 2. Some movies or shows aren’t available on the kids profile even though it is very kid-friendly. I know they technically can’t fix my main problem, but my statement stil stands! 👇

Change the way your house holds work, I travel for work and am away from home very often and sometimes for long periods. Make it so I can select which accounts I want to be able to use while traveling! My family should’ve be able to watch at home while I’m on the road. I get that you want to stop people from sharing there accounts with everyone. But this is very annoying for us who don’t share our accounts and want to use Netflix on the go. I like Netflix it’s probably my favorite steaming service but this makes me want to cancel my subscription! For example if you pay for an account with four devices, you should be able to select four devices that can be used anywhere. Then with that same account set a home IP address that you can use as many devices as you would like. For example your home computer the tv in the living room and the tv in the basement or the one upstairs in your room. This would allow all family members at home to still be able to watch. While also letting four and only four devices to be used any where. The same would go for if you only payed for 2 devices you could only use 2 devices anywhere! Also keep the vacation mode I think that’s a good feature! I am very disappointed in this update Netflix I hope you actually read this and any other comments/reviews because this makes me hate a platform I love!

I don’t ever write reviews, but I’m tired of this. I am a college student in Nebraska, by I’m from Indiana and that is my permanent place of residence. I have always been connected to my parents’ account because we use it as a household. This was never a problem before I went out to school and Netflix decided to change to their one household in one location thing. Now, even though I’m a part of my parents household, I can’t get on our Netflix to watch things when I’m at school because I’m not home once a month, it is too far to make it for a weekend and too expensive. I’m very disappointed because I loved Netflix and some of my favorite things to watch are on there. I am not a separate household but since I spend most of the year at school, it considers me to be and won’t let me use our account. This should be changed. Either change that policy or make a way for college students who are still a part of their parents’ household to still use their Netflix account that they have at home.

They need to work on massive issues with content. They put out so many new series that they wind up canceling a show that is actually popular because it isn’t being viewed enough when it is released. Next thing you know the show is gone after a couple of seasons. They often abruptly cancel them because they believe the show wasn’t watched enough upon release. It’s a streaming platform, people will often finish watching one series before starting another one. It’s frustrating to the customer that is paying for those service to follow specific series only to be left with, yet another incomplete show stuck on a never ending cliffhanger. It’s like a bad relationship that ended with 0 closure, but it happens over and over again. I’ve lost count of how many series I’ve enjoyed for a season or two that has been abruptly ended with out resolution. I mean it happens on all platforms and networks, but Netflix has made it an art. Don’t commit to watching anything on this platform because you will be left wanting!

reviews.x: I very very rarely complain but holy cow. I’ve been trying to help my grandmother with her Netflix account. She canceled her account a while back but they’re still charging this sweet old women. When she called, I witnessed multiple customer service reps lie and put her through the wringer. They asked her for her medical records? If she is able to walk outside? Can she feed herself? They did not know I was on the line. Once I got involved and asked what those questions had to do with cancelling the subscription they doubled-down and continued to lie! They hung up on us 4 times and our issue was never resolved. Netflix hired a bunch of crooks and they’re abundantly aware of it. She has been calling for months to tell them they’re still charging her and nothing has been done. Netflix is disgusting for taking advantage of an elderly woman. I’m still in disbelief of what I witnessed. They were intentionally trying to confuse her. A women who needs that money after just having open heart surgery. So reader, I highly recommend reaching out to your elderly loved ones and see what subscriptions are robbing them blind. It is disheartening to know even Netflix lost their morals to a dollar.

reviews.t: The downfall of a once great platform
reviews.x: First they upped they’re rates but for what they had to offer it was worth it mainly. Then they make it impossible or rather HIGHLY inconvenient to access your family’s account if y’all aren’t on the same WiFi which means the Netflix subscription I got through our shared phone plan is useless because we don’t all live together. Plus with a majority of the shows and movies worth watching being blocked if you don’t pay extra, why would I waste my money and time going through your system. They’re simply making they’re app more exclusive to people who can pay for their inflated rates that allows them to churn out terrible original dramas no one asked for with a low turnout rate as far as quality entertainment. Most of the things people watch from Netflix are only because they’re so bored watching all the old shows over and over again they just don’t even care about the risk of watching a show with a lack of creative writing bc they’ll just jump ship and try the next one. Until they fix this sign in issue OR widen the access to shows again (which they’ll never with established subscription levels), this platform is dead, and only usable for people entertaining their kids at home while they go watch whatever 5-10 season show on Netflix they like for the 5th time.

The amount of money Netflix saves on the cost to produce their original content in a foreign language can’t be worth it. They have to pay to have it dubbed in English which adds to the final production costs as well. The biggest cost to them though is on the consumer end as I’m certain many people simply turn the Netflix original movie off when they immediately realize the film wasn’t originally made in English. It unfortunately makes the movie look like a low budget film and I’m confident many others turn it off just as I do as it’s REALLY HARD to watch. This is very disappointing as lots of the Netflix Original Movies seem to have a terrific plot and they simply don’t get the recognition they deserve as most people won’t give them a chance. This is all because someone at Netflix thinks it’s smarter business to produce these movies in a foreign language and dub the primary language in. This is such an idiotic decision that’s costing the company much more in the long run.

Netflix's recent decision to incorporate ads has significantly diminished the user experience. What was once a haven for uninterrupted binge-watching has transformed into a platform with intrusive commercial breaks. As a paying subscriber, it's disheartening to see the service deviate from its initial promise of an ad-free environment. The flow of a series or movie is constantly disrupted, making it harder to immerse oneself in the narrative. It feels like a step backward, reminiscent of cable TV's approach, where viewers are forced to endure advertisements despite their subscription status. Moreover, the introduction of ads raises questions about the value of the subscription. Users expect to pay for quality content without the annoyance of commercials. Netflix's move seems to prioritize ad revenue over customer satisfaction, leading to a sense of betrayal among long-time subscribers. The shift from a premium, ad-free streaming service to one that incorporates ads undermines the very essence of what made Netflix appealing in the first place, and it leaves users questioning the direction the platform is headed.

reviews.t: Stellar Programing / Great Interface / Decent Support … bring it to Apple Vision Pro.
reviews.x: The quality of shows, movie selection, and original content have truly reached an awe-inspiring high on multiple levels. Wednesday, the Brothers Sun, Rebel Moon, Umbrella Academy, Stranger Things, Nimona, the Sandman, the Witcher, One Piece, Emily In Paris, Cabinet of Curiosities, Squid Game, etc. Wow. Keep it coming. I can rate and favorite things with ease. Watch on my iPad, iPhone, and Apple TV and let family members use their own profiles so they can do the same. I love that I can get to what I want in just a few clicks/taps, and see previews of the movie or show after a few seconds without tapping on anything. I know the Apple Vision Pro is pretty much here… and some folks may be bitter that Netflix is not supporting it at this time. I feel their frustration, especially if they are shelling out $3400 for an all exclusive/inclusive cinematic experience. I would remind folks that there are so many unknowns about the product, and that market response can be unpredictable at times… I respect Netflix’s decision to wait. But IF Apple Vision revives 3D, and creates ripples that solidify a change in expectations of how we view movies… then I will fully encourage and expect Netflix to get on the boat with Apple’s headset. And with extreme expediency- since it’s competitors are already on board and have a head start. Here’s hoping for an exciting new future in home cinema!

"Dear Netflix, I'm writing to express my deep appreciation for 'Midnight Gospel' and to urge you to reconsider its cancellation. The show is a masterpiece that seamlessly blends stunning visuals, thought-provoking conversations, and a unique narrative style. 'Midnight Gospel' isn't just a show; it's an experience. Duncan Trussell's interviews with various guests provide a refreshing and profound perspective on life, spirituality, and the human experience. The animation style is mesmerizing, creating a visual feast that captivates viewers from start to finish. The show has garnered a devoted fanbase who resonated with its deep, existential themes and artistic brilliance. It's not just entertainment; it's a conversation starter, a journey into the unknown realms of thought. I urge Netflix to recognize the impact 'Midnight Gospel' has had on its audience and the cultural landscape. In an era saturated with content, this show stands out as a beacon of creativity and intellectual stimulation. A second season would not only satisfy the existing fanbase but also attract new viewers eager for meaningful and visually stunning storytelling. Please, Netflix, give 'Midnight Gospel' the chance it deserves for a second season. The world needs more of this unique and groundbreaking series. Sincerely, The Watcher

reviews.t: BRING BACK ANNE WITH AN E
reviews.x: I have multiple reasons why this series should NOT be discontinued. First, it speaks on many relevant topics that we face in this century even if the timeline was over 100 years ago. Second, the story was obviously not ended correctly because they’re were so many unsolved stories and the ending felt rushed, the book didn’t stretch the middle of the story and rush the end making everything to happen at once. Lastly, I believe if you published a new season or maybe even two “Anne With An E” could be considered “better than the book” because as you should know that when you publish a movie or series based off a book they always say the book is better because they’re are details, I believe this series has so much potential to become a extremely popular series because it’s very detailed. We’re all hoping for another episode even if it’s in a few years from now.

My parents pay for a PREMIUM FAMILY account, which is already expensive enough as it is being $24 a month (not to mention that they’ve been RAISING their monthly prices and charging additional prices to be AD free, which was the whole point of Netflix to begin with). I recently moved into a dorm for college and all of a sudden now that Netflix has changed their terms to a “single household” I am unable to watch it on my TV. I contacted their help center today and they said, “I am unable to watch it on my TV because it is not a part of my household, HOWEVER I can watch it on my mobile device. If I wish to watch it on my TV my parents would need to be charged an additional $7.99 a month OR I can create my own account for the cheapest price of $6.99 a month.” I think this is ABSOLUTELY ridiculous because my parents pay for a FAMILY account, so why do I have to watch it on my phone? I have a TV for a reason!***I personally think that Netflix is doing a CASH GRAB because they’re mad that people are sharing the same account in different houses. They want as much money as they can so they’re charging more for “extra member spots” while also trying to make BROKE college students AND younger adults who are still using family accounts to pay for their own account*** Why would I pay for an account that my parents pay for just so my siblings and I can use?! I would just rather not watch Netflix. No other streaming services do this. I am currently talking with my parents to cancel their subscription and pay for a DIFFERENT streaming service that allows us ALL to access it. COMPLETELY DISAPPOINTED

I just recently went from the most expensive plan to the basic plan. We only have 2 devices, and ads don’t bother us, so we thought we’d try to save some money. All is going well, until I realized Picture in Picture does not work on the basic plan. I use this feature often, as I typically put a show on for some background noise while simultaneously doing work on the same screen. It’s absolutely ridiculous to take this feature out. I’m not paying attention to your ads any more or less whether it’s playing in a small corner of my screen, or full screen. I’m also not willing to pay almost an extra $10/month just to have a feature that every other streaming app allows you to have, regardless the plan you are on. I canceled my membership, as I realized I haven’t been watching Netflix at all because of this, and also it is just so greedy to take away a simple feature to make people upgrade their plans. Disappointing, since I was a Netflix member from when they used to mail DVDs.

Netflix was once the only app to comfort travelers or expats far from home. Now, it gaslights customers instead of being honest about the fact that it detects a VPN. Unfortunately, for 1.4 billion residents of some places including the one where many US citizens live, we cannot access the software or shows without a VPN. Thus, even though I am a single user with both a US and Chinese residence, I can no longer access the shows for which I pay the fee. I have canceled and know I’m not the current clientele since they are targeting US-based customers who are over-sharing, but it’s a very backwards-facing stance. Please consider that you are cutting off your nose to spite your face. I don’t want your cheap knockoffs off certain shows that you’ve created; I want the same show I have been bingeing for years! I’ll just buy the show, but really, Netflix. Find a way for US customers abroad to *consistently* access your app. Don’t just mindlessly ban all VPNs.

reviews.t: Household Feature is Selfish and Greedy
reviews.x: This streaming platform had already started to lose a lot of quality shows and fill up with very low quality, low rated movies and TV shows. The streaming platform began relying on a few shows like Stranger Things to hold it together (especially after certain shows like breaking bad ended or the walking dead which kind of fell off). The household feature, however, is the reason I’m leaving this review. I am a college student living several hours away from my family and it doesn’t take this into account. It would rather force me or my family to pay double for this platform which already went up in price to 16 dollars. I’ve seen you can add another person for 8 dollars but it isn’t worth spending over 20 dollars a month when there’s plenty of other platforms that allow both my family and I to stream shows. The least they could have done was limited log ins to a certain number of devices. Honestly it was greedy of them and I can’t help but think it was an act of desperation due to other streaming platforms offering better content.

reviews.t: I’d like to Hide a show forever or filter out certain content
reviews.x: This is a feature that would be great for adults and children. Personally, I’m exposed to content and shows I do not want to see. Even the preview or display of certain shows, I find offensive and they don’t align with my values. I want to make these shows disappear so that Netflix never shows them again. Even when I press thumbs down or “remove from this row” the show is still showing. On my kid profile, if my kid watches something I don’t want him to watch I try to remove it but he finds his way back to it. Ex. Do not show me shows that have to do with “sorcery”. Some people may feel this way about “dating” , “violence”, or “Christmas” etc. this feature could help various users with varying belief systems. You have a powerful platform, business is business. I get it. But this enhancement makes your design more ethical. As a Christian Netflix user, I feel offended and exposed to things I don’t want to see and things I don’t want my child to see even after using rating filters . Thank you.

Hey! I absolutely love Netflix, but unfortunately we had to cancel our subscription because the price went up. I think it’s horrible that a customer for years should have to pay the new prices/month. If money is the issue, maybe implement a process of recruitment. Where you recruit a family and that person who recruits them gets extra benefits…more money for the company and happy customers. I’m in a 6 figure household and the fact that canceling our Netflix account makes our lives less stressful is absurd. Hopefully you all can fix this. I would also like to mention that there are some features that should be added for a better experience. Firstly, a filter for movies you have no intention to watch (like movies in other languages). Secondly, a customer should be able to remove a film from “continue watching” especially seeing how we don’t like watching the end credits to EVERY movie. Lastly, security is everything, so inputting a 4-digit passcode before entering Netflix should be a must! Or before you enter a profile. I’ll look into getting Netflix back in a year or two, in hopes that issues can be fixed.

Netflix in 2022 made OVER 31 billion dollars with over a 6% increase from 2021. YET, they decided that apparently that's not enough growth and they could make way more by hitting families with password sharing! My dad has had a Netflix account since 2006, when streaming became a thing he paid the upgrade fee even though his internet couldn't handle that. But me and older brother weee in high school and he figured we could watch it while at my mom's house. When the limited screen play happened, he paid for the upgrade again to get 4 screens so me, my older, brother, younger brother and himself could have our own profiles and watch wherever we ended up landing after college. Instead of Netflix gaining 3 new customers so only kept my dad, however, he downgraded to only 1 screen instead because there's no point since he lives alone. Good for him, because he's saving $5-$7 a month now. But it's only a matter of time where he cancels as well (at least till I convince him) he still has spotty wifi and has to have Netflix buff constantly to watch and frankly it's not worth $15 for one person. When you're a company making over 30 billion dollars a year PLUS, I think the corporate greed to want to get more is a bit outrageous.
